title: The Art School
victoryHeadline: Caught — turns out her sharpest medium wasn't plaster.
acts: The Academy's end-of-term prize shortlist had gone up that morning, and by early afternoon it had ruined everyone's concentration in exactly the way school gossip does. In the Painting Studio, Everly — the school's longest-serving student, older than the building's wiring — had lowered herself to the floor directly beneath her easel and was defending, to anyone who'd listen, her long-held theory that a painting is only properly judged from below, like scaffolding, or a cathedral ceiling. Two easels along, Ginevra had committed the unthinkable: she had sat down. Hers was the only occupied chair in the entire school, and she wore the fact like a medal, one earring catching the light every time she turned to make her point again. Hartley said almost nothing. He'd spent the better part of an hour at the long table chasing one particular shade of ochre — the one his old teacher used to mix without trying — and was, by his own quiet estimate, nearly there.

Word had gotten around that Veronica's new sculpture was the one to beat, and the Painting Studio argument sharpened accordingly, loud enough that a knot of life-drawing students slipped off the Model Platform to go and watch, leaving Fritz to hold his pose alone on the carpet for a class that had entirely stopped attending it. In the Office, Ben stood close enough to the school's single valuable painting to fog the varnish, recalculating its insurance value upward for the fourth time that hour. In Supplies, Anthony's brush count came up two short yet again, and he was still deciding who to blame when Coralie hurried past the doorway with a pair of borrowed calipers she did not want to explain, having spent her lunch break quietly measuring the Gallery's marble for a correspondence course nobody at the Academy knew she'd enrolled in. Under all that noise, nobody heard anything from the far end of the building at all.

The crash arrived without warning: a single, enormous, architectural sound that rattled the ochre in Hartley's dish and didn't so much as trouble Fritz's pose. A soft fall of plaster dust drifted out through two doorways and settled over the argument, which stopped mid-sentence. Coralie was first to the far room, calipers still in hand; Anthony arrived close behind with his clipboard, momentarily forgetting the missing brushes entirely. What they found there was large, white, freshly toppled, and unmistakably final. The prize shortlist, someone would later note, was now down to one name too few.

whereabouts.A: Anthony spent the afternoon in Supplies matching sable brushes against a clipboard tally that stubbornly refused to add up, wedged between a chair nobody sits in and the easel rack, muttering that something in this building eats brushes.
whereabouts.B: Ben stood in the Office close enough to the school's one genuinely expensive painting to fog the varnish, murmuring replacement figures to himself and revising every one of them upward.
whereabouts.C: Coralie was in the Gallery with a pair of borrowed calipers, taking the measurements of a marble bust for a correspondence course in appraisal she hadn't mentioned to a soul at the Academy.
whereabouts.D: Delilah was in the Sculpting Studio with her glasses pushed up into her hair, running a rag along the base of her own piece and dragging a spare chair over so she could reach the top of it without stretching.
whereabouts.E: Everly, the Academy's longest-serving student, had lowered herself to the floor directly beneath her easel, insisting the correct way to judge a painting in progress is from below, like scaffolding.
whereabouts.F: Fritz held a dramatic reclining pose on the Model Platform carpet for a life-drawing class that quietly wandered off to watch an argument next door, and — professional to the bone — simply kept holding it.
whereabouts.G: Ginevra had done the unthinkable and sat down, the only occupied chair in the whole Academy, and was informing the room at length that standing to paint was a tradition invented by people who'd never tried a chair.
whereabouts.H: Hartley stood at the long table chasing one particular shade of ochre his old teacher used to mix without trying, getting quietly, steadily closer, and saying almost nothing to anybody.
whereabouts.V: Veronica spent the afternoon in the Sculpting Studio finishing the piece already tipped to win the end-of-term prize, a spare chair dragged over to reach its top edge, far too pleased with herself to notice she had company.

reveal: It was Delilah, in the Sculpting Studio, with a shove timed to look like an accident and a chair she'd already dragged over for entirely legitimate reasons. Veronica's piece had been the runaway favourite for the prize; Delilah's own had been called "competent" in the student paper, a word she had not forgiven. So she climbed up, reached across under the pretence of admiring the detail, and gave the twelve-foot plaster figure the kind of nudge you'd give a wobbly bookcase — except this one didn't wobble, it toppled, with the slow, ceiling-shaking finality of a felled monument, and Veronica went down with it. Delilah brushed the dust from her sleeves, straightened her glasses, and told the first person through the door that it must have been unstable on its base all along.

escape.generic: The prize went to nobody that term, the plaster dust was swept into a bin bag marked ARCHIVE, and the real culprit went right on quietly accepting compliments on her most recent work.

byAccused.A: Anthony's audit was still two brushes and one glitter mystery short of a conclusion when they took him in, and nobody at the Academy ever did find out where either had gone.
byAccused.B: Ben's own account to the arresting officer was that a man who accurately values his own paintings is exhibiting prudence, not motive, and that nobody had listened to a word of his insurance research.
byAccused.C: Coralie's correspondence tutor sent two increasingly confused emails asking why she'd missed the marble module, and never did get an answer that made any sense.
byAccused.E: Everly was escorted out still lying on the floor of the Painting Studio, informing the officers, with some heat, that they were viewing the whole situation from entirely the wrong angle.
byAccused.F: Fritz was taken in still holding the pose, and by every account held it the entire way to the station.
byAccused.G: Ginevra's chair sat empty for the rest of term, and the Academy quietly decided that sitting down to paint had been the warning sign all along.
byAccused.H: Hartley's ochre dried on the palette, one shade short of the one he wanted, and nobody at the school had the heart to scrape it off.
